Subject: Request: processor evidence, DPIA summary, and transfer inventory

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this — Carter Bank is running a supplier privacy review ahead of our Q4 rollouts. We need the following evidence to complete our intake:

- Current list of subprocessors with locations and roles (Art.28-related).
- High-level DPIA summary showing the risk assessment results and mitigations tied to processing for our use case.
- A record of processing activities (Art.30) or equivalent register for cloud-hosted inference.
- Confirmation of international transfer mechanisms in place (SCCs, adequacy, or other).
- Any Tiered/Segregation options (Dedicated vs Hosted) and associated contractual controls.

Can you provide these documents or a plan/timeline? We have a live compliance committee next Wednesday and would appreciate materials by EOD Tuesday (2026-09-01). If anything requires a quick call, please propose times.

Also, please include any SOC2/ISO attestation dates and whether you operate any processors in APAC or CN that would affect data residency.

Best,
Kelly

Carter Bank

Hi Kelly — Marissa from Legal here. I attached a condensed DPIA summary in the bank-friendly format (dpia-summary-acme-format.docx) and the Art.28/30 register. A few points to note for Carter Bank's committee:

- Subprocessor onboarding: we require contract flow-downs and an annual control attestation. For subprocessors handling personal data, we enforce encryption-at-rest, minimum access controls, and data segregation policies.
- Transfers: SCCs are used by default for hosted service customers. We have additional contractual options for Dedicated deployments (data residency by region + customer-managed keys).
- Retention & deletion: We support customer retention policies via route-level settings and offer an enterprise option to purge KV caches on demand; documented retention windows are included in the register.
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II report excerpt and our most recent penetration test summary are available under NDA. If Carter requires the full SOC report, we can arrange a controlled upload and NDA signature.

I've included inline notes in the Art.28/30 register about where each processing activity is invoked (ingest, inference, embeddings storage, telemetry). Also flagged three subprocessors that currently have APAC presence — details are in the inventory CSV.

If Carter would like, Sean can run a short technical walk-through of the transfer flows and encryption key management.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the fast turnaround — see you Monday.
